newsitem.title: INDIA: India winter rice harvest seen at 75 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: India winter rice harvest seen at 75 mln tonnes.

text.p: India, aided by good monsoon rains, expects its winter rice output to touch 75 million tonnes, surpassing production in the previous season, a senior government official said on Thursday.
"This year, we hope that the crop will be around 75 million tonnes," R.S. Paroda, director-general of the state-owned Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), told Reuters in an interview.
India produced nearly 71 million tonnes of rice in the 1995 winter season, which starts arriving early in October and continues until late in November.
The country produced around 81 million tonnes of rice in 1995/96 (June-July) crop year.
"Timely monsoons helped the rice crop to develop nicely. It will also be beneficial for the subsequent crops," said Paroda.
He said in the 1995/96 (April-March) financial year, India's rice exports surged to nearly 5.5 million tonnes, above the targeted three million tonnes.
"This year, we expect exports to be roughly between five to six million tonnes because crops are better and there is good international demand," Paroda said.
But industry officials expect exports in 1996/97 to be no more than three million tonnes because of a fall in international demand and uncompetitive Indian rice export prices.
Paroda said India presently held rice stocks of around 27 million tonnes, after meeting domestic demand and physical exports contracted in 1995/96.
Stocks would surge to 30-35 million tonnes when the new crop arrived in October, Paroda said.
Paroda said India's rice production was growing at 2.5 percent a year.
"By the turn of the century, we expect to produce around 92-95 million tonnes of rice annually," Paroda said.
